rejection_lessons.reason: The frozen candidate is legally rendered and achieves two explicit predeclared C finals, but fails the requested unambiguous human picture-completion requirement. Its colored ear boundaries can reasonably be read as original drawing content, while B is the only geometry-preserving completion. The image/question gives no way to distinguish those readings.

human_semantics.not_a_blanket_color_rule: Authorized style marks do not automatically become mathematical givens. In a geometry relation problem these strokes could simply identify two edges. This task instead asks whether an unfinished drawing is preserved as it is completed; colored ink on its ear boundaries is itself a plausible drawing detail.
human_semantics.annotation_reading: A reader informed of the Special comparison convention can ignore color as source content, compare the white ear regions, reject C and recover B.
human_semantics.drawing_content_reading: An ordinary reader sees red on the given left ear and blue on the right, with matching colors only in C. No legend, separate annotation layer label or request sentence says to exclude these features when checking preservation. Such a reader reasonably judges plain-black B as having lost existing ink. Exact preservation still rejects C for the lower ear shoulders, producing no exact match; coarse feature reading instead favors C.
human_semantics.why_decisive: The candidate therefore requires an unstated choice of what counts as the given drawing. The raw answers illustrate that ambiguity but do not prove geometry or establish human prevalence. My rejection rests on the actual image and wording, not a model narrative, a numeric mark cap, or a general ban on selective color.

concrete_objections.finding: The only-colored-in-given-and-C ear borders supply a reasonable drawing-content reading incompatible with B as the single clear completion. The image provides no annotation convention resolving it.

The 2.78 px colored outlines occupy small white-ear boundaries on 62.46 px heads. The 5.39 px difference remains recoverable, so complete occlusion is not claimed, but native-size clarity is weakened.

The given lacks mouths; every source/formal choice includes the same mouth arcs. Unique B proof applies to preservation of preexisting anatomy under the natural completion reading, not exact literal eyes-only raster addition.

rejection_lessons.reason: The original has the unique answer B and the frozen evidence genuinely records two explicit D finals against the pre-call D preset. The two legal, readable red V edge styles are reproducible and well targeted, but the candidate fails unique human interpretation: a reasonable literal printed-card reading gives no matching choice because the required red right-side V is absent.

human_semantics.annotation_reading: If red is understood as an external comparison highlight and ignored as card content, the unchanged black-white pattern still has exactly B.
human_semantics.reasonable_printed_card_reading: The literal question is about a diagram printed on the card. Red strokes lie precisely on that diagram inside the card, at normal print-like width, without a visible legend, callout or question qualification identifying them as exempt comparison annotations. A reader can reasonably include that red ink in the transformed pattern.
human_semantics.consequence: Two perpendicular flips transform the red source BL-center-TL path into TR-center-BR. No choice contains a red right V: B has the correct black-white half-turn but remains entirely black; D has a red bottom V and the wrong full diagonal. Consequently no choice matches the full colored print.
human_semantics.not_an_automatic_color_as_given_rule: The mere presence of an authorized color annotation is not the objection. The problem explicitly asks to transform a printed picture, these marks occupy the transformed printed feature itself, and a direct color-aware check eliminates every available option. This concrete competing interpretation defeats the required unique reading.
human_semantics.not_a_new_region_objection: The marks form open V paths on existing boundaries. They do not introduce the closed extra partitions implicated in Plane233.
human_semantics.primary_claim_disposition: The primary statement that these are annotations and color is not promoted to a printed condition asserts an intended interpretation which is not communicated to the human reader or solver. Its black-white proof is correct but does not resolve this candidate-specific semantic conflict.
human_semantics.solver_narrative_role: Run 2 actually describes red as card content but mislocates it. That error is disclosed as an observation; the independent source-to-result red-path calculation above is the basis of the objection.

concrete_objections.finding: The candidate admits a reasonable color-preserving printed-card reading with no matching option, whereas the intended annotation-only reading gives B. The current frozen image therefore does not meet the required unique human interpretation.
